Some names are prayed for years. That is not a failure.

Many women have carried one name in prayer for years: a son, a husband, a mother. Some quietly wonder whether asking again, after so long, shows too little faith.

It does not. Saint Monica prayed for her son for many years, and the Church honours her for the praying. Long prayer is the usual way of it, not a sign that something went wrong.

A prayer song is that same returning, in a form that keeps. It can be played again tomorrow morning, and the morning after, with the name sung each time.

Coming back to the same name is the devotion.

We cannot promise what God will do. We promise the song.

Nobody can honestly promise a healing, a return or an answer. What can be promised is something to hear and to keep, made exactly as described below.

  • In every chorusEach name is sung in all three choruses. A song for one name carries it at least six times.
  • One verse of ScriptureThe bridge is built on a single verse from the Douay-Rheims Bible, chosen for the intention.
  • About four minutesOne original song, its lyrics written around the name, the intention and the one optional line given in the form.
  • Within 24 hoursSent by email to a private page, to play, download and keep.

Frequently Asked Questions

What makes these songs special?

Each prayer song is written from the answers given in the form. It is a one of a kind gift, rooted in prayer and genuine care.

When does the song arrive?

Within 24 hours of the order, by email and on a private page.

Who and what can the prayer be for?

A husband, wife, son, daughter, grandchild, mother, father or friend, the one ordering it, or someone who has passed. The prayer can be for healing, protection, strength, peace, a return to the faith, a marriage, comfort in grief, or thanksgiving. It is a prayer for those things, and no song can promise an outcome.

How is the finished song delivered?

An email arrives with a link to a private page. The song plays there, beside the full lyrics and a button to download the MP3 to keep.

May it be played at church or at a gathering?

Yes. It may be shared with family and played at church, at a funeral or memorial, or at any private gathering. For music during a Mass itself, the parish priest has the final say.

The prayer is already being said. This keeps it.

Many mothers and grandmothers have carried the same name in prayer for years. One song sets that name down, so the prayer can be played and prayed again, by her and by everyone she shares it with.

Three short steps begin it, and they take about a minute. The song arrives within 24 hours, and 30 days stand behind it.

We believe a prayer that is sung keeps being prayed. So Sanctoria sets a loved one's name and a verse of Scripture into a song, to be kept and prayed again.
